Direct standardization over an arbitrary standard population

Source: R/standardize_logistic_fe.R
direct_expectation.Rd

For each provider effect \(\gamma_i\), the expected number of events \(E_i = \sum_k N_k\, \mathrm{expit}(\gamma_i + \eta_k)\) over the rows of a standard population with linear predictors \(\eta_k\) and trials \(N_k\), and \(V_i = \sum_k N_k\, p_k (1 - p_k)\). The direct standardized rate is \(E_i / \sum_k N_k\); its delta-method standard error with \(\hat\beta\) held fixed is \(V_i / \sum_k N_k \times se(\hat\gamma_i)\).

Usage

direct_expectation(gamma, linear_predictor, n = 1, threads = 1)

Arguments

gamma

provider effects.

linear_predictor

\(Z\hat\beta\) of the standard population's rows.

n

number of trials per row of the standard population (default 1).

threads

number of OpenMP threads.

Value

A data frame with expected and variance, one row per element of gamma.

Examples

direct_expectation(c(-1, 0, 1), linear_predictor = rnorm(100))
#>   expected variance
#> 1 28.08335 17.26296
#> 2 47.48502 20.64803
#> 3 67.36212 18.19297
